notes: Two regimes: (1) cheap short-circuits when checks=true — `textbook` (undirected path, min-degree=1) returns in 222 ns; `layered` (directed, not strongly connected) returns in 2.6-34 µs scaling with SCC O(V+E). (2) Fixed-vertex loop fires on rings + complete graphs (connected + min-degree>=2 leave the result undecided, and edge_connectivity has no complete-graph shortcut per flow.c:2168-2180 because multigraphs admit lambda > n-1). On sparse rings C6/C8/C12 cost 2.5/4.3/8.4 µs (linear in V — each FL-011 call on unit-cap sparse graphs runs Dinic in O(E) with a 2-augmenting-path cutoff). On dense K4/K6/K8 cost 1.3/4.5/8.5 µs — slightly cheaper per-vertex than rings because each augmenting path is shorter, but V-1 calls vs. V-1 calls. Compared to FL-015's `pairwise_loop_ring/C12` at 1.4 ms, FL-016 is ~170× faster on the same C12 fixture because the fixed-vertex loop runs V-1 max-flow calls instead of V(V-1) — the asymptotic advantage of computing global connectivity via fixed-vertex iteration instead of all-pairs. Captured with --quick (single sample-set per fixture); for stable medians use the default profile.
